title: Curried Millet Pilaf with Raisins, Almonds and Herbs
summary: Fragrant curried millet is studded with sweet raisins and toasted almonds for a light, warmly spiced pilaf served with a cooling spoonful of yoghurt.

ingredients.item: spring onions, whites and greens sliced separately
millet, rinsed and dried on a tea towel
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast Spices
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large saucepan on medium and cook the spring onion whites with 1 tsp curry powder until fragrant, about 1 minute.

steps.title: Toast Millet
steps.text: Add 270 g rinsed and dried millet and toast, stirring, until lightly browned, about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add 720 ml water and ¾ tsp salt, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer on low until the water is absorbed, 15-20 minutes.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Off the heat, use a fork to fold in 4 tbsp chopped basil and/or mint, 40 g raisins, 25 g toasted flaked almonds and the spring onion greens.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Season with ¼ tsp pepper and serve with a spoonful of yoghurt on each portion.

tips: Dry the rinsed millet on a tea towel before toasting so it browns rather than steams.
Toast the millet briefly in the spiced oil to bring out a nuttier flavour before adding the water.
Fold in the herbs and raisins off the heat so they stay fresh and don't overcook.
storage: Keep in a covered container in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat with a splash of water, adding the yoghurt fresh. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
